coverage_summary:
Independent, read-only round5 review of the actual uncommitted working tree at /Users/addomam/projects/amux-acp-build, using the frozen e04s01-round5-source.json scope rather than HEAD alone. Read the complete assignment, security-review skill, false-positive/confidence references, threat model and approved story/integration contracts. No independent reviewer report was opened.

Verdict: no actionable correctness or security defect at confidence >=8/10 was identified in the reviewed e04s01 scope. Static-review confidence: 8/10. Findings: zero must-fix, zero should-fix, zero consider items meeting the reporting threshold. No actionable Fowler smell identified.

Coverage of the fixed 32-item grid:
1. Exact target tuple: traced target/instance/connection/session parsing and equality through inspect and mutation commit.
2. Opaque control provenance: traced minted capability lookup, kind checks, target binding and server-derived controller identity.
3. Atomic authority/admission: current control is rechecked under the target mutex enclosing broker commit.
4. Captured generations: caller generation is retained and compared with the authorized generation; no current-token substitution.
5. Immutable accepted work: transport consumes admitted frames without later-owner authorization checks.
6. Duplicate calls: lifetime tombstones survive completed-work eviction; normal admission preserves a final close slot.
7. Foreground semantics: one active prompt, explicit busy rejection, no steering or implicit queue.
8. Async startup/FIFO: open reserves authority before worker launch; initialization/new-session responses share the ordered consumer.
9. Negotiation: official pinned v1 schema, version validation and absent unsupported client capabilities.
10. Explicit authentication: only advertised agent-type methods are admitted; unknown discriminators are not silently treated as supported agent auth.
11. Response binding: exact outstanding RPC mapping and session validation; updates are not assigned to prompts by arrival time.
12. Outcome truth: observed response/error, delivery evidence and unresolved-loss unknown remain separate.
13. Explicit interrupt: exact foreground prompt validation; notification submission is not confirmed cancellation.
14. Force/cancel: shared authority transitions retain ACP work; force does not send cancel or terminate the adapter.
15. Publication/close races: startup and consumer publication use the lifetime ordering point; close prevents session resurrection.
16. Owned cleanup: traced setsid, birth-qualified ProcessTree capture/signalling, pinned-child capture-failure cleanup and outside-lock reap/join; uncertain cleanup remains charged.
17. Frame cap: accumulation is bounded before extension, including newline; partial EOF and malformed input fail explicitly.
18. Queue budgets: ingress accumulation, consumer-owned frames and writer-owned frames remain charged; fallible reservations precede action publication.
19. Stalled transport: dedicated writer and stderr drainer avoid pipe I/O under authority/application locks; transport failure remains explicit.
20. History/cursors: bounded event retention, eviction gaps, pagination through-cursors and local cache reconciliation.
21. Privacy: followed prompts, updates, provider errors and stderr into their projections; public metadata excludes conversation content/raw provider errors; content requires explicit inspect opt-in.
22. Inert rendering: reviewed broker sanitization, bounded conversation rendering, label admission and native chrome filtering; no automatic URL/tool delegation sink.
23. Draft identity/revocation: first-edit binding includes exact target/control/generation; changed authority or identity discards rather than rebinds.
24. Input gating/no replay: traced keys, paste, mouse, focus, resize, picker and double-prefix paths; active ACP events do not fall through to PTY forwarding.
25. Local rejection recovery: only synchronously unqueued owned envelopes can restore matching prompt drafts; queued transport uncertainty is not replayed.
26. Canonical status: reviewed capture notices, superseded local errors and canonical work/outcome rendering independently of local queue admission.
27. Native provenance: view/activity/keep/consent require the original live attachment connection; ACP selection carries target-kind facts.
28. Locks: traced authority-to-broker ordering, released-topology projections and cleanup; no new reverse lock edge or blocking transport I/O under admission locks identified.
29. Regression quality: inspected real-daemon/stdio fixture tests, effect counters, held-response barriers, cleanup-before-fallback/sentinel assertions and the production-consumer lifetime race. That race dequeues a charged response while the real target lock is held, then ends the lifetime before application; it is not a post-reap non-event.
30. Legacy boundaries: reviewed native routing rejection, separate agent_views topology and shell-only close/remove; stock Zsh/OMP and legacy agent operations are not replaced.
31. Scope/dependencies/design: schema-only dependency is exactly pinned; no added SDK runtime, generic provider framework, hidden retry policy or persistence path.
32. Evidence/docs/gates: reviewed public usage/changelog, failing story/task status, frozen manifest and parent-produced CLI/PTY evidence. Decoded before/after frames distinguish an unavailable first-read cache from a retained same-view cache; final recovery preserves history/draft, with deliberate Enter alone producing the next recorded effect. Queue-rejection frames show retained text and truthful completed canonical status.

This is static review, not independently exercised runtime verification, complete-story/all-ACP acceptance, live-provider/auth/model approval or publication authorization. The parent-reported 341-test verification was not rerun or independently certified. Historical review caps and native-fence limitations are unchanged.

deferred.reason: All build, lint, test, formatter, runtime, model, authentication and network execution was deliberately skipped as required. Parent-produced evidence was inspected as recorded evidence only; no payloads were executed, credentials inspected, or source/report/index/session/global state changed.

Forms, permission-choice UI, complete interaction-race acceptance and real Codex/Claude adapter/provider compatibility belong to later stories and separate approval gates. Unsupported s01 requests and the implemented late-permission cancellation path were reviewed; later functionality is not approved by this result.

The review covers affected source and nearby shared controls, not the entire unchanged repository or dependency implementation closure. Frozen SHA256 values and reported toolchain/test results were read but not independently recomputed.

Applied the same-user/non-sandbox threat boundary and supplied security exclusions. Resource correctness was reviewed, but DoS/resource-only behavior, theoretical PID/validation races, dependency age, secured on-disk secrets and documentation/test-only issues were not promoted into security findings. No claim repairs or waives the inherited native terminal application fence.
